title: Stedi Actions Inbox

claims.claim: The Stedi Actions Inbox is where every webhook from Stedi lands: file failures, transaction responses, enrollment updates.

checks.note: the webhook receiver would type file-failure events

claims.finding: Every webhook is logged, but only two kinds get an event_type the inbox reads: an 835 ERA notice (typed transaction.processed, backend/supabase/functions/sync-stedi-responses/index.ts:207) and a 277CA that needs a biller (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediAckImport.ts:403). All other events, including file failures and enrollment events, are logged with a blank event_type (sync-stedi-responses/index.ts:207) and the inbox lists only the four typed values (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-list/index.ts:43-48), so they never appear.
claims.proposed_text: The Stedi Actions Inbox shows Stedi webhooks that need a biller's eye: 277CA claim rejections and 835 remittance (ERA) notices.

claims.claim: It is a triage surface — one row per event, with assignment, notes, resolve, and dismiss.
Open it at Billing → Stedi Actions.
Every event Stedi sends via webhook is recorded and shown, filtered to your facility.

checks.note: every event would keep its own type so the inbox could show it

claims.finding: Every event is recorded in stedi_webhook_log, but events other than ERA notices and 277CA rejections are stored with a blank event_type (backend/supabase/functions/sync-stedi-responses/index.ts:207) and are not shown (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-list/index.ts:43-48, 125). Shown rows are filtered to the facility (index.ts:132).
claims.proposed_text: Every Stedi webhook is recorded. The inbox shows the ones Medipyxis marks as needing attention, filtered to your facility.

claims.claim: There are four event types: file.failed, transaction.processed, enrollment.rejected, enrollment.task.assigned.

checks.note: a writer for the three non-transaction types

claims.finding: The filter offers four types, but nothing at v1.1.345 writes file.failed, enrollment.rejected or enrollment.task.assigned; only transaction.processed rows are created (see sai-01).
claims.proposed_text: The Event Type filter lists four types (File Failed, Transaction Processed, Enrollment Rejected, Enrollment Task). At this release only Transaction Processed rows are created.

claims.claim: transaction.processed — A payer response came back for a claim you submitted. Includes 999 (acknowledgement), 277CA (payer receipt/reject), 271 (eligibility response), 835 (remittance advice).
claims.finding: Only 835 and 277 transactions are recognised (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediInboundEvent.ts:33-38); 999 and 271 events are logged untyped and never shown. A 277 is shown only when it needs a biller (backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediAckImport.ts:403), so 277CA acceptances do not appear either.
claims.proposed_text: transaction.processed — a 277CA that rejected a claim you submitted, or an 835 remittance (ERA) notice.

claims.claim: file.failed — Stedi rejected the submitted 837P outright. enrollment.rejected — A payer refused an enrollment request. enrollment.task.assigned — Stedi opened a manual task on a payer enrollment.

checks.note: these rows would have to be written to appear

claims.finding: These event types are never written at v1.1.345, so these rows cannot appear (see sai-01).
claims.proposed_text: File-failure and enrollment events from Stedi are recorded but do not appear in the inbox at this release.

claims.claim: Medipyxis stores the event, resolves it to your facility, links it to the affected claim or enrollment when it can, and puts it in this queue.
Every row starts in Open.
In Progress — someone assigned it to themselves or added a note. The row is being worked.

checks.note: assign AND note would both set In Progress

claims.finding: Only Assign sets In Progress (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-update/index.ts:145). Adding a note does not change status (lines 175-187).
claims.proposed_text: In Progress — someone assigned it. The row is being worked.

claims.claim: Resolved — the underlying issue is fixed. Dismissed — the event is not actionable.
Filters at the top let you scope by status, event type, payer, and assignee. Default view is Open across all types.
Claim link — when the event references a submitted claim, the row shows the patient name, the claim's local status, and the payer name. Click through to open the claim detail.

checks.pattern: 'id, claim_number, patient_name, status, local_status, stedi_status, payer_name, facility_id'

claims.claim: Enrollment link — when the event references an enrollment, the row shows the payer, the transaction type, and the current status.

checks.pattern: 'stedi_enrollment_id, id, payer_id, transaction_type, status, status_text, facility_id'

claims.note: Display code exists; enrollment events are not typed at this release (sai-07), so in practice no row carries an enrollment link.

claims.claim: Affected claims count — for file.failed events, how many claims were in the rejected file.
Raw payload — the original Stedi webhook body, unmodified, for reference or to send back to Stedi support.
Assign — Puts the row in your name. Sets status to In Progress. Others still see it — assignment is not exclusive.

checks.note: the list is per facility, not per assignee

claims.claim: Assign, Note, Resolve and Dismiss: any biller. Unassign: the assignee or admin.
claims.finding: No role or assignee check exists for any action: every action except stamp_facility only requires access to the facility (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-update/index.ts:109-112). Unassign is offered only in the bulk bar that appears when rows are ticked (frontend/src/pages/StediActionInboxPage.tsx:546-553).
claims.proposed_text: Anyone with access to your facility's billing can Assign, Unassign, Note, Resolve and Dismiss. Unassign is in the bar that appears when you tick rows.

claims.claim: Unassign — Removes the assignment. Returns the row to Open if no note or resolution is on it.
claims.finding: Unassign always sets Open and clears resolved_at/resolved_by, whatever notes exist (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-update/index.ts:150-155).
claims.proposed_text: Unassign — Removes the assignment and returns the row to Open.

claims.claim: Note — Adds a comment on the row without changing status. Notes are stacked chronologically and stamped with author + time.
claims.finding: Notes are appended with a timestamp only; the author is not recorded (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-update/index.ts:186).
claims.proposed_text: Note — Adds a comment on the row without changing status. Notes are stacked in order and stamped with the time (not the author).

claims.claim: Resolve — Marks the row Resolved with a resolution note. Records who resolved it and when.

checks.pattern: return json({ error: 'action.resolution_notes is required for resolve' }, 400, corsHeaders);

claims.claim: Dismiss — Marks the row Dismissed with a reason. Same audit shape as resolve.
claims.finding: Dismiss takes no reason: the modal sends none (frontend/src/pages/StediActionInboxPage.tsx:896-898) and the function stores only status, resolved_at and resolved_by (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-update/index.ts:167-171).
claims.proposed_text: Dismiss — Marks the row Dismissed and records who dismissed it and when. No reason is asked for; add a Note first if you want one on record.

claims.claim: Resolve and Dismiss both take a required note. That note is the audit trail.
claims.finding: Only Resolve requires a note. Also, Resolve replaces the stacked notes with the resolution note (backend/supabase/functions/stedi-action-update/index.ts:164), so earlier notes are lost; and bulk Resolve writes the fixed text "Bulk resolved" (frontend/src/pages/StediActionInboxPage.tsx:558).
claims.proposed_text: Resolve requires a note. Dismiss does not. Resolving replaces the row's earlier notes with the resolution note.

proposed_checks.pattern: return json({ error: 'action.resolution_notes is required for resolve' }, 400, corsHeaders);

claims.claim: Occasionally an event arrives from Stedi without a facility link. When that happens, no biller sees it in their facility's view. Ask Medipyxis support — they can attach it to your facility.

checks.pattern: stamp_facility requires superadmin or customersupport role

claims.claim: When a transaction.processed event carries a 277CA rejection for a claim, the claim's Stedi status updates from submitted to the payer's specific state (accepted, rejected on the 277CA, paid, etc.).

checks.note: an 835 would move the claim to paid

claims.finding: The 277CA sets the claim to accepted or rejected (backend/supabase/migrations/20261019160000_stedi_277ca_claim_status.sql:136-143, called from backend/supabase/functions/_shared/stediAckImport.ts:214). An 835 never sets 'paid'; ERA posting only writes ledger rows.
claims.proposed_text: When a 277CA arrives for a claim, the claim's status moves from submitted to accepted or rejected.

claims.claim: The claim appears in the Work Queue under the appropriate bucket ("Needs biller attention" for a rejection, "Paid" when an 835 arrives).
claims.finding: No Work Queue bucket named "Needs biller attention" exists in frontend/src, and an 835 does not set the claim to paid (see sai-25).
claims.proposed_text: A rejected claim shows status rejected in billing; an 835 posts its payment to the claim's ledger.

proposed_checks.pattern: const ledger = eraId ? await postEraToLedger(supabase, eraId) : null;

claims.claim: The event stays in the Actions Inbox as the audit record of when the response arrived and what it said.
File.failed with "structural validation error" — the 837P payload was malformed before it reached the payer. Open the claim, check the fields called out in CMS-1500 and 837P fields, resubmit.

checks.note: file.failed rows would need a writer

claims.finding: file.failed rows are never created at v1.1.345 (see sai-01), so this pattern cannot appear in the inbox.
claims.proposed_text: Stedi file failures do not appear in the inbox at this release; check the claim's submission result on the claim page.

claims.claim: 277CA with a payer-specific reject code — the reason code (from the AAA segment) tells you why: AAA*Y*72 is subscriber-not-found, AAA*Y*73 is patient-not-found, AAA*Y*79 is transaction-not-supported.

checks.note: the inbox would read an AAA segment

claims.finding: The inbox Reason column shows the 277CA STC status as category:status code (frontend/src/pages/StediActionInboxPage.tsx:139-147); no AAA segment is read. AAA is the 270/271 eligibility reject segment, not part of a 277CA, and in the X12 AAA03 list 72 = invalid/missing subscriber ID, 73 = invalid/missing subscriber name, 79 = invalid participant identification (X12 code list; not encoded in the product).
claims.proposed_text: 277CA rejection — the Reason column shows the 277CA status as category:status code (for example A7 with its status code). Fix the field the code names on the claim and resubmit.

claims.claim: Enrollment.rejected with "Provider not enrolled with payer" — the provider needs to enroll directly with the payer before Stedi can register the enrollment.

checks.note: enrollment.rejected rows would need a writer

claims.finding: enrollment.rejected rows are never created at v1.1.345 (see sai-01). The payer-enrollment advice itself is external process guidance.
claims.proposed_text: Enrollment rejections do not appear in the inbox at this release; check the Enrollment page.

claims.claim: Copy the event ID (top of the expanded panel), the event type (from the row), and the timestamp when the event was created.

checks.note: event ID shown in the expanded panel

claims.finding: The expanded panel does not show the event ID (frontend/src/components/stedi-actions/StediActionExpandedRow.tsx); it is only searchable (frontend/src/pages/StediActionInboxPage.tsx:188) and is in the raw payload. The row shows a friendly event label (e.g. "Claim rejected"), not the raw type, and the received time ("Webhook received").
claims.proposed_text: Copy the event's id from the raw payload, the received time (Webhook received), and the raw payload itself.

claims.claim: The raw payload (there is a copy button in the expanded view).
claims.finding: There is no copy button; the raw payload is a collapsible text block (frontend/src/components/stedi-actions/StediActionExpandedRow.tsx:250-263).
claims.proposed_text: The raw payload: open Raw Payload in the expanded row and select the text to copy it.

claims.claim: Stedi support looks these up by event ID.
